title: Prove direct and MCP harness execution parity in an isolated offline fixture
goal: Vision: V-6. Make the next capability-preserving boundary concrete with one actual accepted task and no-replay evidence through existing harness_run/runs/status; retain every current implementation and access policy.

reuse.searched: harness capability inventory at core-100k-boundary-state; tests/gmcp_requirements/support.rs StdioSession; susi-harness/tests/mission_no_replay.rs; xtask/src/local_workflow/tests.rs real native gate fixture; existing operator/daemon harness implementation
reuse.reason: Exercise current production implementations using local deterministic provider, real native coordinator and isolated Git/board/state; no production replacement or dependency required.

constraints: No external board/provider traffic; fixture environments cleared and remotes asserted local.

results.validation: passed: 1 opt-in integration test, 84.36s; focused clippy with -D warnings; rustfmt; git diff --check
results.baseline: Both isolated repositories ran cargo test and failed only the intended accepted_change assertion (41 vs 42) before inference.
results.accepted: Direct CLI and child-process MCP each performed two fake-provider inference calls, passed native acceptance and produced an integration receipt/ref containing the exact fix while preserving main and the test.
results.parity: Initial report, complete ledger rows except timestamps, skipped replay report, zero replay calls/spend, MCP status done=1 failed=0 calls=2 cost_micro_usd=30.
limits: Opt-in Linux execution experiment, not release qualification or extraction.
No dedicated MCP harness_command/harness_cancel_run tools; cancellation parity not proven.
Socket executable override specifically rejected; direct CLI executable configuration remains unchanged.
Explicit paths supplied; CLI/socket default-state-path difference remains.
No license, access, install, dependency, production behavior or core-size reduction change.
